北.meaning: A <part>climbing pole</part> and a <part>spoon</part> stand back to back, both shivering. They kept walking up the map until the snow reached their knees and a polar bear started staring at the spoon. They've gone too far <kanji>north</kanji>.
北.on: To warm up, they share a <sound>ho</sound>tdog with a frozen <sound>cu</sound>ckoo.
北.kun: The spoon digs up a frozen <sound>key</sound> sticking out of a <sound>tu</sound>b of snow.

西.meaning: A flat bar on top, then a box with two legs dangling inside, like a traveller hanging in a doorway. Every evening he watches the sun sink, then walks after it, always toward the <kanji>west</kanji>.
西.on: He carries his gold in a little steel <sound>sa</sound>fe strapped to his back.
西.kun: At sunset he kneels, one k<sound>nee</sound> in the dust and a <sound>shee</sound>p beside him, to watch the sun go.

自.meaning: An <part>eye</part> with a little tuft of hair on top stares into a mirror for hours, combing the tuft. It takes a selfie, then another, then ten more. It only ever looks at one thing: <kanji>oneself</kanji>.
自.on: It even paints its own face on the side of its <sound>jee</sound>p.
自.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat carves its own face on a <sound>zu</sound>cchini, then on a <sound>ca</sound>rp, then cheers for itself: '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

見.meaning: A huge <part>eye</part> walks around town on two skinny <part>legs</part>. It doesn't talk or eat. It just stops and stares at everything: shop windows, clouds, your lunch. All it wants to do is <kanji>see</kanji>.
見.on: It walks up to the <sound>ken</sound>nel and stares at the puppies for an hour.
見.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> stare right back at it.

南.meaning: A <part>ten</part> signpost points the way above a big <part>frame</part> of a beach hut. Inside, a goat with <part>horns</part> hangs wet swimsuits on a <part>drying rack</part>. It's hot, the sea is warm and everything dries in a minute: you've come far <kanji>south</kanji>.
南.on: The goat bakes a puffy <sound>naan</sound> on a hot stone in the sun.
南.kun: On the hot sand, a <sound>mee</sound>rkat hands a <sound>na</sound>an to another <sound>mee</sound>rkat.

斗.meaning: Two dots beside a cross with a long handle: a ladle for scooping water. Look up on a clear night and seven stars make the same shape, a giant ladle hanging in the sky. It's the <kanji>Big Dipper</kanji>.
斗.on: A <sound>to</sound>tem pole points up at the stars, its top carved like a ladle.

料.meaning: A canteen cook weighs one <part>ladle</part> of <part>rice</part> onto a tray, and the tray stays locked until a coin clinks into its slot. No coin, no lunch: every ladle has its <kanji>fee</kanji>.
料.on: At the <sound>ryo</sound>kan, the rice at dinner costs extra: one coin per ladle.

有.meaning: A <part>slash</part> and a <part>one</part>-plank arm make a hand that reaches up and grabs the <part>moon</part> right out of the sky. 'Mine now,' says the hand, tucking it under its arm. There's only one moon, and he gets to <kanji>possess</kanji> it.
有.on: A <sound>u</sound>nicorn gallops up and asks to borrow the moon for one night.
有.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' he says. 'Look, <sound>Roo</sound>, I have the moon!' and shows it to his kangaroo.
